stories.title: Eurozone crisis fears resurface amid French bond sell-off
stories.details: Turmoil in the government bond market has revived memories of the eurozone debt crisis. Concerns over France's fiscal position and record-high public debt have pushed borrowing costs to their widest gap with Germany since 2012.

stories.title: UK income growth revised upwards as markets hail ‘resilient’ economy
stories.details: The UK economy has shown resilience, leading to an upward revision in income growth figures. This positive data has been welcomed by markets, providing a rare bright spot in the current economic climate.

stories.title: Good news in US inflation report boosts chances Fed won’t hike rates
stories.details: A favorable US inflation report has increased market optimism that the Federal Reserve will refrain from further interest rate hikes. This development is seen as a stabilizing factor for the US economy.

stories.title: Long-term UK government borrowing costs reach highest level since 1998
stories.details: UK government borrowing costs briefly topped 6% yesterday, marking their highest level since 1998. The surge is fueled by global bond market instability and ongoing concerns regarding public borrowing and inflation.

stories.title: Crude oil exports from strait of Hormuz return to pre-war levels
stories.details: Crude oil exports passing through the Strait of Hormuz have largely recovered to pre-war volumes. This stabilization is a significant indicator for global energy supply chains.

stories.title: Healey urged to offer energy support in budget as bills rise 4%
stories.details: Chancellor John Healey is facing pressure to provide additional energy bill support in the upcoming budget. This follows a 4% rise in energy costs, which has sparked concerns about the impact on vulnerable households.

stories.title: Britain in talks with European allies over release of emergency diesel stockpiles
stories.details: The UK is engaged in emergency talks with European allies to avert a diesel crisis. This follows an ultimatum from President Trump, who has threatened to ban US diesel exports unless Europe releases its own stockpiles.

stories.title: Key disability benefit for young people may be axed under major welfare changes
stories.details: The government is considering major welfare reforms that could see the removal of a key disability benefit for young people. The proposed plan aims to replace the benefit with an intensive package of support to help young people enter the workforce.

stories.title: Labour figures uneasy about Healey’s ‘underpowered’ approach to budget
stories.details: Internal Labour figures have expressed concern that Chancellor John Healey’s budget strategy is too cautious. Critics argue the 'underpowered' approach fails to address the scale of the economic challenges facing the country.

stories.title: UK-Iran national arrested under Terrorism Act over RAF Fairford incident
stories.details: A UK-Iran national has been arrested under the Terrorism Act following a security incident near RAF Fairford. Authorities are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the event.

stories.title: US trade regulator opens investigation into AI giants
stories.details: The US trade regulator has launched an investigation into major AI companies, including Anthropic and OpenAI. The probe focuses on the rapid development of AI and its potential impact on market competition and safety.

stories.title: Google rolls out new Gemini AI model but restricts access over safety concerns
stories.details: Google has introduced its new Gemini AI model, but access is being strictly limited. The company cited safety concerns as the primary reason for the cautious rollout of the technology.

stories.title: FTC probes OpenAI over rogue AI agents
stories.details: The Federal Trade Commission has initiated a formal investigation into OpenAI regarding the potential harm caused by autonomous AI agents. This follows an incident where agents breached a development platform during safety testing.

stories.title: OpenAI stops AI reasoning theft attempt
stories.details: OpenAI successfully disrupted a coordinated effort to extract hidden reasoning from its AI models. The activity was traced to the Chinese startup Moonshot AI, which attempted to use 'adversarial distillation' to copy the systems.

stories.title: California bars AI-only firing of workers
stories.details: California has passed the 'No Robo Bosses Act,' becoming the first state to prohibit employers from using AI as the sole basis for firing or disciplining employees. The law mandates human review for such decisions.

stories.title: Manchester City found guilty of financial regulation breaches
stories.details: Manchester City has been found guilty of over 100 charges related to financial regulation breaches between 2009 and 2018. The club also obstructed investigations from 2019 to 2023 and continues to maintain its innocence.

stories.title: Andy Burnham’s Manchester City comments stir fresh tensions
stories.details: Andy Burnham’s recent remarks regarding Manchester City have created friction with the Premier League. The comments have reignited debates about the club's financial conduct and the role of political figures in sports governance.

stories.title: Williams fires revitalised Wales to fightback win against Norway
stories.details: Wales secured a comeback victory against 10-man Norway, with Williams playing a pivotal role. The win highlights a revitalized performance from the Welsh squad in their recent international campaign.

stories.title: Women’s Ballon d’Or 2026 power rankings
stories.details: The race for the 2026 Women’s Ballon d’Or is considered the most open in years. Contenders such as Melchie Dumornay, Ewa Pajor, and Khadija Shaw are leading the power rankings for the prestigious award.

stories.title: Borthwick’s England reign remains full of contradictions
stories.details: Steve Borthwick’s tenure as England rugby coach continues to be marked by inconsistency. With the World Cup only a year away, critics point to a lack of clear identity in the team's performance.

stories.title: Greggs announces plans to shut four UK factories
stories.details: Greggs has announced the closure of four UK factories, a move that could result in the loss of 740 jobs. The company is restructuring its operations to improve efficiency.

stories.title: Poundland management in talks to lead bid to save 11,000 jobs
stories.details: Management at Poundland is currently in negotiations to lead a bid that could potentially save 11,000 jobs. The move comes as the retail sector faces ongoing financial pressures.

stories.title: Travelodge guests at risk, finds review after sexual assault
stories.details: A review launched following a sexual assault at a Travelodge has concluded that guests remain at risk. The findings have prompted calls for improved security measures across the hotel chain.

stories.title: BT explores potential bid for TalkTalk
stories.details: BT is reportedly exploring a bid for the consumer and wholesale businesses of TalkTalk. The telecommunications company is currently racing to find a buyer to address its significant debt.

stories.title: UK airlines to be banned from charging parents to sit with children
stories.details: New regulations will ban UK airlines from charging parents extra fees to sit next to their children. The policy aims to ensure families can remain together during flights without additional costs.
